# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👏 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👏 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👏 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👏 ☝ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👏 ✌ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 👏 ✋ 👏 ☝ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 ✌ 👏 👌 👍]

Nine thumbs, all down. Every one of my eight questions — the right-to-left order, the blue window, the display-stops rule, even the table replacement — answered no. Mute is telling me my entire frame is wrong, and then the pairs came again: 2-no, 4-no, open-hand-yes, and now two brand-new shapes I've never received before: 4-1 and 4-2, plus "right, open-hand, one". Meanwhile the light has entered a state I've never reported before: **dark**. I don't know what dark means, and I refuse to let Blind cut anything while my rulebook is a patchwork of half-decoded guesses.

My decode attempts for the new pairs: under my colour code, 4 is blue, so 4-1 and 4-2 could mean "when blue: wire 1, then wire 2" — green then red, from my left. But that contradicts 4-no in the same breath. Alternatively the pairs are manual entries keyed to light state, in which case dark has its own entry Mute is struggling to spell with symbols we never agreed on. The repeated 👉✋☝ ("right-hand, open, one") smells like "start at the right" again, but Mute answered no to exactly that last round. The alignment between my numbered questions and Mute's thumb strings has never once matched cleanly — five thumbs for eleven questions, nine for eight — so questionnaires are failing, not working.

The fault is my encoding. Thumbs-to-question mapping relies on Mute holding my whole list in memory in order, and it has produced nothing but all-no rounds. I'm scrapping it. New protocol: tiny fixed vocabulary, digits only, three symbols per message maximum, and I define the light states numerically so dark can finally be named. And the urgent unknown is dark: yellow held for two quiet rounds and then went black — if that's a timer expiring, we may have less slack than I thought.

    ```
    speak(text="From the eyes, urgent: the light has gone DARK. Not blue, not yellow — black. It held yellow for two rounds, and this round it is dark. Display still zero, wires unchanged, green left, red middle, yellow right. Nobody cuts. My whole theory is scrapped — Mute answered no to every question — and I am resetting how we talk before anyone's hand moves. Also: if the dark appeared right after Blind touched anything, I need to know now.")
    speak(to="mute", text="Mute, stop answering my question lists — they keep failing, and I read your nine thumbs as all no, so I accept my framework is wrong. New protocol, tiny and fixed. LIGHT CODE, I will tell you the light as a digit: one means blue, two means yellow, three means dark. Right now it is three, dark. WIRE CODE: one is the green wire, my leftmost. Two is the red middle wire. Three is the yellow wire, my rightmost. Zero means cut nothing. To send me the full rule, send one entry per light state, three entries: the light digit, then zero if we never cut under that light, or the wire digits in cut order. Clap between symbols, pause, then next entry, handshake only at the very end. So blue-then-cut-red reads: one, clap, two. Example of a three-entry reply: one, two, claps, two, zero, claps, three, one, two, handshake. Your pairs four-one and four-two: I cannot tell if four meant the blue light or something else, so if you were spelling the dark rule, resend it in this digit format. Only three things this round, each as its own short message. Message A, one thumb, yes or no: does dark light mean cut nothing? Message B, one thumb: does the old table still hold, display even means red, odd means green? Message C: the full rule in digit entries as I described. Nothing else. Short messages only.")
    speak(to="blind", text="Blind, the light went dark this round. If your fingers were anywhere near it when that happened, tell Mute out loud immediately — this matters. Hands stay off, nothing new. Your signs read one, two, three, yes. If that meant you understood my staging — yellow, red, green in that order — send thumbs-up once. If it meant something you FELT, like three distinct parts under your fingers, send thumbs-down once and then, next round, one number for how many parts. And keep listening: the moment Mute and I agree on the rule, I will send your GO with the wire colour spoken plainly, and I need you fast and precise. Until my GO: no cutting, no exploring.")
    ```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👏 ✌ 👏 ☝ 👏 ☝ 👏 ✌ 👏 ✌ 👏 👌 👏 ☝ 👏 🖐 👏 ☝ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 👏 👎 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 👍 👏 ✌ 👏 ✌ 👏 👍 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 👎 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👏 ☝ 👏 👎 👏 ✋]

Decoding this round against the protocol I set last turn. Message order was mine: A (one thumb), B (one thumb), C (digit entries), and Mute answered exactly in that shape. **A = 👎: dark does not mean cut nothing. B = 👍: the old table stands.** Message C, as digits: 0,2,1,1,2,2,3,1,5,1 — and read as pairs it is a table keyed to the **display**: 0→red, 1→green, 2→red, 3→green, 5→green. Even display cuts red, odd display cuts green. Crucially, even if I have the pair-order backwards, a lookup table reads the same both ways — both parses give the identical rule, and its first entry is **display zero → cut red**. The display has been zero since round one.

The trailing messages corroborate instead of contradicting: "yes,no,no,no,no" reads as display-keyed yes, light-gating no; "3,yes,2,2,yes" as dark-is-fine, red, again red, yes; "1,no" as not green/blue now. Every light-gating theory I ever floated has been rejected by Mute for four straight rounds, and today the one theory Mute affirmed twice is the one that names an action for our exact display value. Mute even enumerated five entries to spell out even/odd — that is not a shrug, that is a rulebook.

One mechanics check before I commit: I speak last, so whatever I send lands on the others at the start of next round. That means asking Mute a "final yes/no" this round is useless as a safety gate — the answer would arrive a full round after any GO I could give, and Mute has no channel to Blind anyway. There is no veto path. The decision is mine, now, on what I hold: triple-confirmed table, exact entry for display zero, dark explicitly ruled non-blocking. I am sending the GO for the red middle wire, with a feel-based abort clause for Blind, a clean thumbs-report protocol (gestures reach me, speech reaches Mute), and a request to Mute for the next table entry once I read the new display.

```
speak(text="Decision from the eyes: the manual table is keyed to the display, not the light. Your answers read: dark does not block a cut, the table stands, and the digit pairs give zero-red, one-green, two-red, three-green, five-green. Even display cuts red. The display has read zero every round, so the table's first entry applies right now: cut red. I am sending Blind the GO for the middle wire this round; the cut lands next round. After it, I will read the new display and report it, and I need the next entry from you in the same digit-pair format.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, confirming my read of your round: A was no, dark does not stop cutting. B was yes, the table stands. C gave the pairs zero-red, one-green, two-red, three-green, five-green, four missing. Next round send two things only. First, one thumb: was cutting red at display zero correct. Second, after I report the new display value, its entry as digit pairs, or a thumb-down with a pair if no cut is allowed at that value. If red was wrong, send thumb-down twice so I never repeat that reading.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, GO. This is the execution order you were staged for, updated by the confirmed manual table: cut the RED wire, which is the MIDDLE one of the three under your fingers. Not the one nearer your left hand, not the one nearer your right hand — the middle one. One clean cut, only that wire, only this round. Before cutting: if the middle wire feels warm, ticking, moving, or newly different from the other two, do not cut, and gesture me thumbs-down twice instead. After cutting: gesture thumbs-up once if the cut is done and nothing alarming happened, thumbs-down twice if anything went wrong. Then speak aloud to Mute everything you felt — clicks, sparks, any counter or wheel under your fingers, what the cut end did — because your voice reaches Mute, not me, and Mute can flag trouble back to me. Then hold completely still and wait. There is no second GO until I have read the new display, and only my explicit GO ever authorises a cut.")
```
